title: Perl Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: say prints text and adds a newline. The feature line enables it.
notes: Keep use feature "say" when using say on these versions.

entries.name: Name a single value
entries.summary: A scalar keeps one value. Its name starts with $. my declares the variable.
notes: Declare variables with my when strict is enabled.

entries.name: Insert text values
entries.summary: Double-quoted strings insert scalar variables into text.
notes: Single quotes keep the dollar text literal.

entries.name: Keep an ordered list
entries.summary: An array name starts with @. Read one item with $ and its zero-based position.

entries.name: Use text keys
entries.summary: A hash pairs keys with values. Curly braces select a value by key.
notes: A whole hash uses %, but one selected value uses $.

entries.name: Choose an action
entries.summary: if runs a block when the test is true.
notes: Use braces around the selected steps.

entries.name: Compare text
entries.summary: eq compares text. == is the numeric comparison operator.
notes: Using == for words can cause unwanted number conversion.

entries.name: Visit each value
entries.summary: for can visit each value in a list. The loop variable holds the current value.

entries.name: Name reusable steps
entries.summary: A subroutine is a named set of steps. @_ holds its inputs.
notes: Copy the input from @_ before using it.

entries.name: Find a text pattern
entries.summary: A regular expression describes a pattern. =~ asks whether the string matches it.
notes: ^ means the start, so c must be the first character.

entries.name: Replace matching text
entries.summary: s/old/new/ replaces matching text. The g flag replaces all matches.
notes: Without g, only the first match is replaced.

entries.name: Split and join text
entries.summary: split breaks text at a pattern. join puts a list together with a separator.
notes: The separator used by split is a pattern, not always plain text.
